text:
Likewise, in the <term>Ratnakūṭa Sūtra</term> <gloss>The Heap of Jewels Scripture</gloss> <note>original: "Ratnakūṭasūtra"; see the same text cited below regarding chapter 17, verse 33</note>: At that time, those five hundred <term>bhikṣus</term> <gloss>monks</gloss> <note>The Tibetan translation adds "who had attained meditative absorption"</note>, not penetrating, not diving into, and not finding faith in the Lord's teaching of the <term>Dharma</term> <gloss>the Buddha's Law</gloss>, rose from their seats and departed.

Then the Lord, at that moment, magically produced two <term>bhikṣus</term> <gloss>monks</gloss> on the path by which those monks were traveling.

Then those five hundred monks approached the place where those two <term>nirmitakas</term> <gloss>magically created beings</gloss> were. Having approached, they said: "Where are you venerable ones going?"

The two created monks replied: "We are going to the forest retreats. There we shall dwell in the comfortable state of the bliss of <term>dhyāna</term> <gloss>meditative absorption</gloss>. For as for the <term>Dharma</term> which the Lord teaches, we do not penetrate it, we do not dive into it, we do not find faith in it; we are alienated, we feel terror, and we are falling into panic."

Then those five hundred monks said this: "Venerable ones, we also do not penetrate, dive into, or find faith in the Lord's teaching of the <term>Dharma</term>. We are alienated, we are terrified, and we are falling into panic. Therefore, we too shall dwell in the forest retreats in the comfortable state of the bliss of meditation."

The two created monks said: "In that case, venerable ones, we shall agree and not dispute. For the qualities of a <term>śramaṇa</term> <gloss>ascetic seeker</gloss> consist primarily of <term>avivāda</term> <gloss>freedom from dispute</gloss>." <unclear>******</unclear> <note>See below at folio 100a; the text here is abbreviated</note> "For the sake of abandoning what, venerable ones, have you set out?"

They replied: "We have set out for the sake of abandoning lust, hatred, and delusion."

<summary>This page quotes the Ratnakuta Sutra to illustrate monks who, unable to grasp the Buddha's profound teachings, are met by magically created monks who guide them toward tranquility and the abandonment of defilements.</summary>
<keywords>Ratnakuta Sutra, monks, dhyana, meditation, nirmitaka, non-dispute, śramaṇa, abandoning defilements</keywords>
